newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-EU wheat cut seen defusing subsidy issue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-EU wheat cut seen defusing subsidy issue.

text.p: The cut in European Union (EU) wheat subsidies had reduced the prospect of possible U.S. wheat subsidies becoming an issue during next week's talks between Australian Prime Minister John Howard and visiting U.S. President Bill Clinton, Australian trade officials said.

Officials in Howard's office were not immediately available for comment but in the recent days have declined comment on specific trade issues which could be raised in the Australian leader's talks with Clinton.
Clinton begins a five-day tour of Australia on Tuesday and will meet Howard and other Australian leaders in Canberra on Wednesday.

Australia's Primary Industries Minister John Anderson told a news conference in Rome on Thursday that Australia hoped the EU and United States would not get into a subsidy war after the EU restored subsidies on wheat exports.

But Alex Nichol, communications manager at the Australian Wheat Board said much of the sting had gone out of the subsidy issue with the EU's subsidy reduction on Thursday to 22 Ecus per tonne from 27 Ecus.
The EU also seemed to be very conscious of subsidy issues with the present United Nations-sponsored World Food Summit in progress in Rome, he said.
Nichol also commented that while the Australian wheat harvest was slow to get into full swing this year, any recent downgradings of the crop because of recent rain had not been severe.
"There are no disasters around," he said.
